idea: Policy risk monitoring for renewable energy investors
pain: Subsidy and policy changes destroy returns and arrive with little warning
v1: A monthly policy risk monitor across three jurisdictions
verdict: Sticky subscription and a real budgeted need; the differentiation against existing providers is the question.

why.distribution: Renewable infra funds are reachable through her network.
why.demand: Funds pay for policy monitoring today from several providers.
why.fmf: Policy interpretation plus investment framing; her China access is only partly relevant to European policy.
why.revenue_structure: Annual subscription that embeds into risk processes.
why.defensibility: Coverage and consistency matter more than uniqueness here.
why.tailwind: Policy volatility in energy is genuinely elevated and consequential.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/mo x 14 funds = £202k. Fourteen infra fund subscribers is plausible but requires displacing incumbent monitoring services. Realistic: 5-6 = £72-86k.
carries: Excellent leverage and revenue structure with a genuinely consequential need.
kills: Undifferentiated. Several firms already do policy monitoring competently.
test: Ask four renewable funds what policy monitoring they buy and what it costs.
test_pass: They describe gaps, especially outside Europe.
test_fail: They are content with what they have.
